newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gerling takes full control of Namur units.
newsitem.headline: Gerling takes full control of Namur units.

text.p: German insurance group Gerling AG said on Tuesday it had bought up the shares it did not already own in Namur Kreditversicherungs S.A. of Belgium and Namur Rueckversicherung of Luxembourg.
Gerling had bought 73 percent of the companies -- a credit insurer and reinsurance group -- in 1994.
In a statement, Gerling said the full takeover reinforced its claim to be Europe's leading credit insurer and underlined its increasingly international orientation.
Gerling said more than half of its premium income was generated abroad. The company now had subsidiaries and branches in 13 European countries and in the U.S.
